chapter_title: Concerning the Four Things over which People kill
spiritual_reading:
The first corruption is that the human will becomes fixed on gratifying the outer self, so that the delight of bodily life is made the ruling end and the mind is driven to seek satisfaction for its own enlargement rather than for use.

The second corruption is that the marriage of good and truth within the mind is profaned, and the power of conjunction is turned into promiscuous union; thus the affection that should be made chaste by wisdom is cast into disorder, and mutual relation is reduced to the commerce of mere appetite.

The third corruption is that external acquisition is loved for its own sake, and the possession of means is exalted above the ends they were given to serve; thus what is without use is called good, and the self takes honor to itself from what it has gathered.

The fourth corruption is that the love of dominion is kindled, so that minds enter into contention, accusations, and assaults of judgment against one another; and when one prevailing will overthrows another, rule is exercised as tyranny, and reputation in the external community is sought as a final reward.

All who attach themselves to these four ruling loves, which are made common speech and common desire in the natural degree of life, strive with one another to bring them forth into act and to multiply them within their societies.

Yet the Divine brings a discernment into the mind that makes a real distinction between what is from heavenly love and what is from infernal love, and so sets what is true and living apart from what is false and deadly.

For such corruptions cannot remain conjoined with what is eternal; they are therefore separated and cast off, and the life that made them primary comes to its end, because what is severed from heaven has no enduring being.

fills.notes: The oldest layer is describing the first ruling love: fixation of the will on bodily delight. “Obsession” is too modern-psychological; the substrate register typically names this as desire or lust (a ruling end) for eating and bodily life.

Correspondentially the body’s “swelling” is the drive to enlarge the outer self. “Increase” fits the impersonal, cosmological register better than a medical image, while preserving the meaning of self-enlargement.

fills.fill: so that their thought is made heavy and their soul becomes forgetful
fills.notes: After “eat for the increase of their body” the teaching typically states the spiritual effect: the mind is dulled, interior remembrance is lost. This matches the spiritual translation’s point that the mind is driven and reduced to outer gratification.

The second ruling love is the profanation of conjunction. In the oldest layer it is stated as impurity or defilement, not moral exhortation. This clause supplies the general heading before the repeated instances of fornication.
Pairs naturally with “fornication” in this register as the general forms of unchaste conjunction; also matches the spiritual sense of profaning the marriage of good and truth.

Completes the series “fornication … fornication … men and women …”, making explicit the disordering of relations in every direction, as demanded by the correspondential description of promiscuous union.
Balances the previous item and keeps the impersonal catalogue style of the oldest layer.
The third ruling love is external acquisition for its own sake. “Gathering” expresses the act of accumulation in the natural degree, corresponding to exalting means over ends.
The contrast in the sentence is between “useless riches” and what they lack “from it”; correspondentially this is the absence of use (end-service) from possessions.
The fourth ruling love (dominion) unfolds as contention, accusation, and judicial assault. “Disputes … accusations … trials” is the demanded sequence in the spiritual translation.
These ruling loves become “on every tongue in the world” not only as speech but as public approval. This keeps the external-community emphasis of the oldest layer (reputation as reward).
The striving to generate and multiply these loves occurs within social bodies; “assemblies” fits the impersonal societal register without importing later ecclesial language.

fills.fill: But the Judge of the worlds comes between them,
fills.notes: The spiritual translation requires an agent that introduces discernment and separation. In the oldest substrate this is not a Christian title but a cosmic function: the ordering Judge who distinguishes and divides Light from Darkness.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored at the level of the correspondential structure (the four ruling loves; their social multiplication; the cosmic separation of Light and Darkness; the non-endurance of corruptions). Several short lacunae in ¶2 and ¶6 admit more than one equally plausible Coptic phrasing; the restorations given aim to stay in the impersonal, cosmological register of the oldest substrate and avoid later moralizing or ecclesial terminology.
